newsitem.title: TANZANIA: 400,000 Rwandan refugees on the march in Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: 400,000 Rwandan refugees on the march in Tanzania.

text.p: Some 400,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees have abandoned their camps in northwestern Tanzania and were trying to trek to neighbouring countries after defying orders to go back to Rwanda.
Refugee agency officials said there was no doubt the latest move by the refugees was well-organised and coordinated by refugee leaders in the camps.
Aid workers quoted refugees as saying they planned to go to bordering Malawi, Zambia, Kenya or Uganda.
In Geneva, a U.N. refugee agency spokeswoman appealed to Tanzania not to use force against the columns of Hutu refugees winding into the bush.

Tanzania had informed the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees that Rwandans outside a four-km (two miles) parameter of the camp were subject to prosecution, according to the UNHCR spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole.
"UNHCR appeals to the Tanzanian authorities not to use force. UNHCR believes that these people are still refugees and should be treated as such," O'Toole told Reuters.
She added that U.N. refugee chief Sadako Ogata had started urgent contacts with high-level Tanzanian officials on the latest Central African refugee crisis.
Judith Melby, a spokeswoman for the UNHCR in Ngara, said heavily-armed Tanzanian troops in the area had so far made no efforts to intervene.
Melby said the refugees were marching in an orderly manner, heading in the same direction.

The refugee exodus came shortly after Rwandan military strongman and Vice-President Major-General Paul Kagame ended talks in Kampala with President Yoweri Museveni on the refugee issue and civil war in Zaire.

"They also discussed the conflicts in Burundi and Zaire and stressed the importance of continuing to work together as a region in efforts to help the peoples of the two countries to resolve the conflicts," the statement issued by the presidency in Kampala said.

On the other side of Rwanda in Zaire, where up to half-a- million other Rwandan refugees may be adrift in equatorial forests, Zairean rebels declared a unilateral ceasefire in their campaign to overthrow the government in Kinshasa.
In Benaco refugee camp in Tanzania, once the largest in the country with 160,000 to 180,000 Rwandans, only a few stragglers lingered in the debris on Thursday night.

The rest of the refugees disappeared into the distance like ants on the march -- old men, children and even the maimed, loaded with mattresses, their other meagre possessions and blue plastic sheeting from their huts in the camp.
"I'm leaving because some of the refugees repatriated yesterday were killed in Rwanda. I'm sure if I go back I will be killed also," said a refugee who gave his name as Theoneste.
The U.N. officials said the five other camps in the area were also deserted, giving a total of between 400,000 and 500,000 people on the loose in the Tanzanian bush.
The exodus started on a small scale last Sunday and began to snowball as word spread through the camps that refugees in other areas had headed out.

Members of the Hutu militia, the Interahamwe, do not want to go home for fear of prosecution or reprisals for the massacre of Rwandan Tutsis in 1994. They also want the other refugees to stay with them on the grounds there is strength in numbers.
UNHCR had hoped it and the Tanzanians could persuade the refugees to go home willingly, following the example of more than 600,000 who have gone home from Zaire since mid-November.
Instead the plan seems to have backfired.
